title: Jets July Invitational 2026: MAGA Sweeps Six Divisions as BTYC Rules the All-Around
subtitle: MLC's team posts the field's top score in Level 7 Division 1, and two gymnasts move closer to a division promotion after clearing the cutoff score for the second time this season
tldr: Melbourne Acrobatic Gymnastics Academy (MAGA) won six of the Jets July Invitational's fifteen team events across Levels 3 to 7, while BTYC Gymnastics answered with four individual all-around titles on top of four team wins of its own. MLC's Level 7 Division 1 squad posted 143.1 to top its field, with Kristen Canoy edging teammate Miranda Hale by just 0.15 for the all-around title. Host club Jets Gymnastics fielded more teams than any other club, 14, backing up its own report that entries filled within a day of opening and some sessions drew more than 190 spectators. Elsewhere, BTYC's Elisha Choi and MAGA's Peyton Baldwin have each cleared the cutoff score for the second time this season, putting both in line for a possible promotion.

title: Inside Chamford Gymnastics: Two Level 9s, One National Medal, and an AIS Callup
subtitle: A Murrumbeena club since 1982, headlined this year by Estelle Warnes and Lexi Thomas, who went unbeaten and runner-up across the Level 9 Division 1 circuit before Lexi took national silver on beam and both were picked for the AIS International Pathways Green Camp
tldr: Chamford Gymnastics Club has been a Murrumbeena fixture since 1982, no closures, no rebuilds, in a series where most clubs have moved, closed, or rebuilt at least once. In my database, 52 WAG athletes compete under the Chamford banner. Estelle Warnes went unbeaten across all five of her Level 9 Division 1 starts this season, including two 26-athlete statewide fields, and Lexi Thomas finished runner-up in three of her own five. Both then went to the Australian Championships in June, where Lexi won national silver on beam, and both have since been selected for the AIS International Pathways Green Camp in August. A third athlete, Mia Bell, has climbed from Level 5 to Level 7 over three seasons and was named to the Level 7 Border Challenge squad.

title: Niddrie Invitational 2026: MAGA Sweeps Level 4 Division 1 as Edge Posts the Day's Best Vault in Division 3
subtitle: Niddrie fields four teams in a Level 3 Division 2 field decided by just 0.4 points, while Edge Gymnastics matches Melbourne Acrobatic Gymnastics Academy's best score of the competition to win Level 4 Division 3
tldr: Gymnastics Victoria still hasn't published official results for the 11-12 July Niddrie Invitational at the time of publishing, so we reached out to Niddrie Gymnastic Club and Melbourne Acrobatic Gymnastics Academy (MAGA), and both clubs emailed over the official scoresheets. MAGA's Level 4 Division 1 team swept every apparatus and the all-around title. Its Level 4 Division 2 team backed that up with wins on bars, beam and floor, though Niddrie's third-place team took out the Div 2 vault with a 27.6. Over in Division 3, Edge Gymnastics posted the competition's best vault score, 28.7, to win it outright. And in Level 3 Division 2, host club Niddrie fielded four separate teams in a field decided by just 0.4 points across the top three.

title: BTYC MAG Junior Invitational 2026: Host Club Wins Three All-Around Titles and Two Team Crowns on Home Turf
subtitle: Harley Fehily-Lewis sweeps every apparatus at Level 1 Under, Zach Zweck edges Jackson Cohoe by 0.025 at Level 2 Open, and Rian Chan caps a Level 4 Under win with the competition's highest single score
tldr: BTYC Gymnastics hosted its MAG Junior Invitational on 26 July, drawing ten clubs across Levels 1 to 4 for 117 individual all-around routines. The host club had the best day of any, winning three of the competition's eight individual all-around titles and two of its six team titles. At Level 1 Under, Harley Fehily-Lewis won the all-around and swept all six individual apparatus outright. At Level 2 Open, Zach Zweck held off Jackson Cohoe (MYC Gymnastics) by just 0.025, the tightest margin of the day. And Rian Chan's Level 4 Under win came with a 10.15 on pommel horse, the highest single score of the competition.

title: Y Invitational 2026: Strive's Pippa McLeod Edges Teammate Allira Brown by 0.025 in the Tightest Finish of the Weekend
subtitle: Strive sweeps the top four in Level 6 Division 3, host Geelong YMCA Gym Club dominates its own floor with four team titles and the Level 7 Division 1 and Level 7 Under all-around crowns, and Niddrie sweeps the Level 6 Division 1 podium
tldr: The event continues to grow, 12 clubs and 222 individual all-around entries this year. The tightest finish of the weekend came in Level 6 Division 3, where Strive Gymnastics' Pippa McLeod edged teammate Allira Brown by just 0.025, with Strive taking the entire top four. On its own floor, host Geelong YMCA Gym Club won four of the weekend's sixteen team titles and the Level 7 Division 1 and Level 7 Under all-around crowns. Niddrie Gymnastic Club swept the top four individual places in Level 6 Division 1 and filled eight of thirteen spots in Level 5 Division 1. Mildura Gymnastics Centre made the long trip from the state's north-west and posted results across four levels over both days.

title: Inside Eureka Gymnastics: The Regional Circuit
subtitle: A Level 10 gymnast, a 2026 Level 9 state title, and a State Team reserve, all from a Ballarat club that closed once, moved twice, and is about to host its own regional invitational again
tldr: Eureka Gymnastics Club has been part of Ballarat's sporting life since 2007, pausing operations in 2010 while it transitioned to become a fully independent club, reopening in 2013, then moving twice since, into a bigger purpose-built shed in 2015, and again into its current home on Grandlee Drive, Wendouree, earlier this year. In my database, 43 WAG and 5 MAG athletes compete under the Eureka banner. Layla Muir has climbed all the way to Level 10 and finished 2nd at this year's Senior Victorian Championships, Myah Johnston won the Level 9 Division 2 title outright at the same event, and Eloise Murphy was named a Level 9 Open Reserve to this year's Victorian State Team. In a few weeks, Eureka hosts the Eureka Invitational again at its new venue, with five other regional Victorian clubs making the trip.

title: Knox WAG Junior Invitational 2026: Indiana Beach Edges Vivienne Soldo by 0.05 as MAGA's Depth Carries the Team Results
subtitle: Home favourites sweep the Level 7 Division 1 podium, MAGA banks six of the weekend's sixteen team titles on the back of a Niddrie sweep the week before, and three athletes turn last year's rock-bottom finishes into wins
tldr: Knox Gym Club hosted its WAG Junior Invitational over the weekend of 18-19 July, drawing 20 clubs across Levels 3 to 7. The tightest margin of the day came in Level 5 Division 2, where Indiana Beach (Cheltenham Youth Club) edged Vivienne Soldo (Essendon Keilor Gym Academy) by just 0.05. On its own floor, Knox went 1-2-3 in Level 7 Division 1 through Lara Thorn, Saisha Bowman, and Emma Curlis, plus the team title. Melbourne Acrobatic Gymnastics Academy (MAGA) won six of the weekend's sixteen team titles, more than double any other club, continuing a run that included a Level 4 team sweep at the Niddrie Invitational the week before, results Gymnastics Victoria still hasn't officially released. Niah Vanzin, Chelsea Hassell, and Chloe Baker all turned rock-bottom finishes from earlier in the season into Knox wins.

title: Inside Athleta Gymnastics: Young Guns
subtitle: Founded in January 2018, one of only two clubs in this series under a decade old, and already good for a State Team selection, a Border Challenge pair, and a Developing International Squad spot this year
tldr: Athleta Gymnastics opened in Altona North on 23 January 2018, making it, along with MAGA, one of only two clubs profiled in this series under a decade old. It hasn't slowed the club down: Ella McGrath earned a Level 9 Open State Team spot this year on an unusual partial-trial selection case, Abigail Alley and Edie Thomas both made the Level 9 Border Challenge team, and Chontelle Burgess was named to the Developing International Squad off the back of an unbeaten 2024 season. In my database, 36 WAG and 5 MAG athletes compete under the Athleta banner. On the MAG side, a small five-athlete squad is anchored by Ryan Voinescu, who placed 2nd at Level 8 at this year's Senior Victorian Championships.

title: Gymnastics at the Movies: My Honest Ranking (and Thoughts on 'Nasty')
subtitle: A gym dad who works in film weighs in on the new Rose Byrne and Jenna Ortega gymnastics drama, then ranks every gymnastics movie he's actually seen
tldr: Warner Bros just announced 'Nasty', a gymnastics drama starring Rose Byrne and Jenna Ortega. A gym dad who works in the film industry breaks down the news, the title backlash, and ranks every gymnastics movie he's actually watched, from Gymkata to Stick It.

title: BTYC WAG Junior Invite 2026: MAGA Sweeps Level 7 as BTYC Wins Three at Home
subtitle: Eastern opens its season with six team podiums, PIT collects gold and silver, and Kotomi Lee leads a BTYC sweep of Level 6 Division 1
tldr: BTYC Gymnastics hosted the 2026 WAG Junior Invite on 12 July, drawing nine clubs across Levels 3 to 7. Melbourne Acrobatic Gymnastics Academy (MAGA) won both Level 7 team titles and swept all seven individual placings in Division 1, where it was the only club entered. Host club BTYC won three team titles on its own floor, at Levels 4, 5, and 6, and swept the individual podium in Level 6 Division 1 through Kotomi Lee and Lauren Kam. Five clubs shared the day's eight individual level titles, MAGA with three, BTYC with two, and one apiece for Athleta, Eastern, and Gymnastics Unlimited. Eastern Gymnastics Club opened its season with team results across six separate divisions, and PIT Gymnastics picked up a team gold and silver at Levels 3 and 4.

title: Inside Knox Gymnastics: One of Victoria's Biggest Clubs
subtitle: From a council-run program in 1972 to roughly 800 members a year, a full Junior Invitational field this weekend, and a Level 10 senior peaking at exactly the right time
tldr: Knox Gymnastics Club has been running since 1972, moving between sites over the decades before settling at its current Wantirna South venue, and by the club's own count now carries around 800 members a year, making it one of Victoria's larger programmes. This weekend Knox hosts its WAG Junior Invitational, covering the full Junior category, Levels 2 through 7, with last year's edition drawing 254 athletes from 19 clubs. In my database, 48 WAG and 20 MAG athletes compete under the Knox banner. Megan Herrmann has gone from a mid-pack Level 10 finish in 2024 to the best score in my database for her, 47.833, this year, and on the MAG side, Joshua Hart stepped up to Level 10 this year after three seasons building a case at Level 9, going 4th in his first start before winning his second with 66.2, the best score in my database for him, while Taylor Sweeny didn't lose a Level 8 competition all of 2025.

title: Warrnambool Invite 2026: Vivien Artz Edges Poppy Kelson by 0.025 as Strive Shines on Home Turf
subtitle: Blue Lake's Holly Lawrence and Chloe Bickley both step up a level, and Millicent makes the trip across the South Australian border
tldr: The 2026 Warrnambool Invite ran on 7 May, hosted by Strive Gymnastics in Victoria's south-west. Vivien Artz edged clubmate Poppy Kelson by just 0.025 in Level 5 Division 1, Strive's Level 6 team posted the highest team score of the day, and Blue Lake Gym Club and Millicent Gymnastics Club both made the trip across the South Australian border.

title: Inside EKGA: The Club Built on a Second Mortgage
subtitle: From salvaged equipment in Airport West to 40 WAG and 32 MAG athletes, 36 combined medals at Level 8 and above, and two national gold medals this year
tldr: Essendon Keilor Gymnastics Academy was founded by Christy Hemphill in November 2005, funded by a second mortgage and maxed-out credit cards, opening in Airport West with salvaged equipment and second-hand mats. Twenty years on, EKGA has 40 WAG and 32 MAG athletes in my database, with 36 combined medals at Level 8 and above across the two programmes. Katia Taranto has anchored the WAG squad at Level 10 across three straight seasons. On the MAG side, Geoffrey Fairservice and Patrick Deane have each climbed to Level 8 since 2024, and per the club's own announcement, both won gold at the 2026 Australian Championships, Fairservice on Rings and Deane on High Bar, a result that sits above anything my Victoria-only database can show.

title: Inside MAGA: Acrobatics, Ambition, and a New Chapter
subtitle: How Stephanie Fuller's long-held dream is taking shape — and how a difficult closure gave it a new dimension
tldr: Melbourne Acrobatic Gymnastics Academy opened in Cranbourne West in August 2018, the realisation of founder Stephanie Fuller's years-long ambition to run her own gymnastics programme. MAGA's acrobatic gymnastics squads were Runners Up for the VIC State Pennant in their first year of competition; by 2025, the Level 9 trio of Tessa Bottomley, Madison Mete, and Brianna Rawlings had won the Senior Victorian Championships outright, and Jana Ametoglou and Lachlan Renwick had swept the Level 6 titles across trials and championships. When Funtastic Gymnastics closed under difficult circumstances in late November 2025, MAGA opened its doors to the displaced coaches and athletes — among them Head Coach Janet Howe, bringing an entire Division 1 WAG programme into a gym that had been ready for exactly this for a long time.

title: Inside PIT: The Club the University Built
subtitle: From a Preston Institute of Technology corridor in Bundoora to 35 MAG athletes, 29 medals at Level 8 and above, and an annual invitational
tldr: PIT Gymnastics in Mill Park takes its name from the Preston Institute of Technology, the Bundoora campus where the club was founded in 1979, an institution that has since become RMIT. Forty-seven years later, the club runs approximately 750 gymnasts across programs from recreational to elite, and the data reflects something unusual for Victorian gymnastics: more MAG athletes than WAG. In our database, PIT has 35 MAG athletes and 23 WAG athletes. The MAG programme has accumulated 29 all-around medals at Level 8 and above, including Conor McGillivray winning the Junior International all-around at the 2025 Senior Victorian Championships with 75.85. At the 2026 Senior Vics, Adam Bowman won the Level 8 Open all-around with 66.6, Jamil Awad placed third and won three apparatus events, and Liam Duncan placed second at Level 6. The club also hosts its own annual MAG invitational, drawing competitors from across the Victorian circuit.

title: Inside The Y: The Club Across the Bay
subtitle: From a woollen mill on Pakington Street to 91 WAG athletes and 11 international-level gymnasts
tldr: Y Geelong Gymnastics has been competing at the Victorian Championships since 1988, and the data reflects what three decades of steady building produces: 91 WAG athletes, 51 all-around medals at Level 8 and above, and 11 athletes who have competed at international levels in our database. At the 2026 Senior Victorian Championships, the club won team gold at both Level 8 and Level 10, with Ivy Alford sweeping the Level 8 individual titles and the international stream producing four medallists on the same day. Their MAG programme, smaller at 18 athletes, contributed a Level 5 Floor title from Hamish Goodin. In the weeks before the championships, the club lost Terry Cliff, the YMCA Executive Director who established the gymnastics programme in the late 1970s and ran the organisation until 2000.

title: Inside MYC: The Club at the End of the Peninsula
subtitle: What 70 years of gymnastics on the Mornington Peninsula looks like in the data
tldr: MYC Gymnastics has been running gymnastics on the Mornington Peninsula since 1954, and the numbers tell a story of quiet dominance: their MAG programme has accumulated 90 all-around medals at Level 8 and above, more than any other Victorian club in our database. Their Level 7 WAG coaching team won Gymnastics Victoria's Coaching Team of the Year. Four athletes qualified for the Level 10 National Squad, with further selections across the Level 9 State Team and Border Challenge squads.

title: Inside BTYC: Victoria's MAG and WAG Double Act
subtitle: The numbers behind one of Victoria's few clubs running competitive programmes at the elite end of both WAG and MAG
tldr: BTYC Gymnastics has been running gymnastics in Melbourne's east for over 60 years, competing seriously at the top end of both WAG and MAG. Their men's programme has accumulated 71 AA medals at Level 8 and above, with nine athletes on the 2026 MAG State Team and head coach Lachlan Graham leading the state coaching staff.

title: Inside Waverley: Victoria's Gymnastics Powerhouse
subtitle: The club that produced Australia's 2025 All-Around champion, sent athletes to the Paris Olympics, and is currently developing 20 international-level gymnasts
tldr: Waverley Gymnastics Centre is Victoria's dominant elite WAG club. With an Olympian, the reigning Australian All-Around champion, 20 athletes at international level, and 27 state team selections in 2025 alone, the numbers tell a story that's hard to argue with.

title: Does Difficulty Actually Win? A Gym Dad Digs Into the Data
subtitle: What 3,400 competition results say about the D vs E trade-off in Victorian WAG
tldr: A data analysis of over 3,400 Level 7+ Victorian WAG results finds that difficulty is a stronger predictor of competitive success than execution on most apparatus, but beam is the exception, elite clubs show no trade-off between the two, and a handful of athletes prove you can win on pure execution alone if it's exceptional enough.

title: Why I Don't Expect My Gymnastics Daughter to Love PE
subtitle: A gymnastics dad wonders whether school sport is really for everyone
tldr: A gymnastics dad whose daughter trains 19 hours a week reflects on why he doesn't mind if she isn't enthusiastic about school sport, and questions whether the assumptions behind mandatory PE fit every student equally.

title: Inside the Numbers: the stats behind Victoria's 2026 team selections
subtitle: A gymnastics parent's look at how trials, apparatus strengths, and championship form shaped who got the call-up
tldr: Using trial and championship data, we break down how Victoria's 2026 WAG State Team and Border Challenge Team were selected, with three clubs (MAGA, Waverley, and YMCA Geelong) each landed seven athletes across the two squads.

title: A weekend to remember: highlights of the 2026 Senior Victorian Championships
subtitle: Maddie Smith claims Level 10 by 0.033, Estelle Warnes stays unbeaten, Cerano Tosone sweeps five apparatus events
tldr: Maddie Smith (Cheltenham Youth Club) claimed Level 10 by just 0.033 points over Annabella Geraghty, Estelle Warnes (Chamford) capped an unbeaten 2026 campaign at Level 9, and Cerano Tosone swept five of six Level 7 apparatus events, a weekend to remember across WAG, MAG, and Acrobatic Gymnastics.

title: Waverley Invite 2026: Eclipse Gymnastics claims Level 10 double as Wawolangi shines on home floor
subtitle: Tight team margins, year-on-year leaps, and skill debuts across two days at Waverley Gymnastics Centre
tldr: The 2026 Waverley Judges Invite delivered on May 10–11, with Eclipse Gymnastics Ringwood's Indianna Gilson and Isobel Myles claiming both Level 10 titles, Estelle Warnes winning Level 9 after a remarkable year-on-year jump, and both team competitions settled by under a point.

title: No, Maria Paseka didn't quit at the Olympics
subtitle: A viral clip from 2012 is missing some very important context
tldr: A widely-shared YouTube Shorts clip claims Maria Paseka 'quit' at the 2012 Olympics, but what you're actually seeing is a deliberate team strategy called a 'scratch', and it was entirely intentional.

title: Nadiu edges Cross by 0.034 at WAG Trial 2
subtitle: Sophie Strano leads a tight Level 8 Division 1 field at CYC, while Emma Hale posts the bars score of the competition
tldr: Arianna Nadiu (MAG Academy) won Level 7 by just 0.034 points at WAG Trial 2 and Border Challenge Trial 2, while Sophie Strano (Jets) led L8 Division 1 with 47.332 and Emma Hale posted a 13.033 on bars.

title: Oceania Selections
subtitle: Australia Names Strong Squads for Home Oceania Championships and International Tour
tldr: Australia has announced full men's and women's squads (senior & junior) for the Oceania Championships in Brisbane, plus selected athletes and coaches for upcoming events in Slovenia and China.

title: Three new Uneven Bars skills
subtitle: Three gymnasts debut original Uneven Bars elements in Osijek, each earning official recognition in the Code of Points
tldr: At the Osijek World Cup, Hamelin (FRA), Mesiri (GRE), and Rodrigues Barbosa (BRA) each successfully performed new Uneven Bars skills, meeting the criteria to have them officially named and added to the Code of Points.
